title: Defense of Sovereignty “Is Not Rhetoric, It’s Principles,” Sheinbaum Says
author: Anahí Del Ángel
content:
_This article by[Anahí Del Ángel](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/anahida/)
originally appeared in the [October 9, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/defensa-de-la-
soberania-no-es-retorica-son-principios-sheinbaum/), an investigative Mexican
news outlet._

The defense of **sovereignty** **" is not rhetoric, it's principles,"** said
President **Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo** , in response to questions about whether
her stance is enough to confront pressures from the **United States**.

During the October 9 morning press conference, the president maintained that
the defense of sovereignty does not constitute an instrument for evading other
issues of the public administration, but rather a principle that must remain
in the collective memory: **" It is part of our history and we must always
defend it."**

In that sense, she recalled that Mexico faced **pressures from foreign
powers** in different episodes, particularly during the 19th and 20th
centuries. For that reason, she stated:

> **A people that has no memory has no compass.**
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

Sheinbaum Pardo questioned the decisions adopted during the **neoliberal
period** , considering that greater foreign influence was then allowed in the
definition of the country's **economic policy**. She also referred to the
government of **Felipe de Jesús Calderón Hinojosa** , whom she blamed for
having allowed **greater participation of U.S. agencies** in Mexican
territory.

In addition, in response to questions about the economic situation and
criticism that the defense of sovereignty would not be enough to confront
external pressures, she replied that her administration is also working on
well-being, education, health, and infrastructure.

She highlighted that **42 million Mexican women and men directly receive
support from the Well-Being Programs**. She also asserted that, by the end of
the six-year term, 400,000 new spaces will have been created in upper
secondary education and 300,000 in higher education.

In terms of health, she noted that her administration is working on the
consolidation of the **Universal Health Service** , through the expansion of
care capacity and the strengthening of prevention actions.

The President of the Republic also defended her administration's
infrastructure program, which she described as **" the most ambitious of any
six-year term,"** with highway, energy, and water projects, including
electricity transmission and distribution networks.

"Mexican women and men know that we work permanently for the people of Mexico,
and for the well-being of all Mexicans," she concluded.
